chapter: Billy Berg's, Granz and Nat Cole
title: The 1944 New York trio and its Exclusive Records songs
summary: Based with family in Brooklyn, his trio with Sir Charles Thompson and Louis Gonsales sang his own songs and recorded for Leon Rene's label.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You were in New York, though. You mentioned something about being there in '44, didn't you.

Yeah, I was there in '44, but I was working out of New York more than... Well, my family lived in Brooklyn, I stayed with them, and I worked out of New York with the group I told you about -- the trio with Sir Charles and Luis Gonsales. Also we used to sing a lot of things. Because I used to write a lot of little songs. Like "Baby, I'm Gone" and stuff like that we used to sing. And we made records of those things. I used to record for Exclusive Records, which was a Leon René company. Herb Jeffries also recorded for them, and I recorded with the trio. A couple of the things I remember was doing "Skyline" and "I Wonder" asnd "Baby, I'm Gone" and "Be Happy, Pappy." Those were some of my original compositions.
I think I might have some old 78's of some of those, year. I think I have some of them.
Those would be fun to hear.
